text: NNSA infrastructure modernization programs is the best and only option to pace projected threats and sustain strategic deterrence.” [HASC, 2022] This DARHT Capability eXpansion (DCX) strategy has been developed to implement NNSA requirements for sustainment and modernization to ensure DARHT continues to serve its role as a weapons mission–critical facility. DCX has three overarching priorities: 1. Extend DARHT’s reliability and resilience 2. Increase the quality and quantity of DARHT data 3. Enable hydrodynamic measurements in complex environments Each priority is briefly described here and further developed in extensive detail in each section of the strategy. These priorities are grounded by the constraint that the facility, supporting facilities, accelerators, vessel confinement systems (VCSs), detectors, and radiographic analysis tools are coupled systems that must work together to create quantifiable, state-of-the-art data sets. Given these complexities, great care is being taken to phase in sustainment and modernization efforts while coordinating DARHT operational and experimental commitments, as well as ensuring current data quality is not only maintained but enhanced. DCX STRATEGY 3 Extending DARHT's Reliability and Resilience After more than 20 years of continuous service, major facility infrastructure systems must be replaced to enable at least two more decades of reliable service. The DARHT facility concrete structures, roof, electrical power, building automation controls, oil system, and water systems each have aging issues that need to be addressed as discrete projects under the umbrella of DCX. To increase resilience, a broad spectrum of advancements is planned to address facility flooding, recurring power outages, and cyber security threats. To enhance security for sensitive experiments, address worker quality of life, and improve data quality, the control and diagnostics rooms will be redesigned and revitalized to modern standards for mission-critical operations. Supporting facilities in the DARHT Complex are typically much older than the DARHT facility and need a broad spectrum of repairs to reliably support DARHT operations and maintenance into the future. New facilities will be constructed, and existing buildings refurbished, to address current VCS operational limits, the lack of space for critical DARHT spares, and temporary office buildings. The accelerators have each accumulated more than 40,000 shots (40,000 for Axis 1 and 43,000 for Axis 2). Vital accelerator main- tenance projects will be leveraged into performance enhancements that will bolster higher quality x-ray beams, translating into better hydrodynamic experiment (hydro) data for customers. Both accelerators need modern diagnostics and control systems to address obsolescence traps. Due to the extensive testing performed prior to installation, Axis 1 (A1) has aged gracefully and will only receive modest refurbishment to aging accelerator systems. Axis 2 (A2) has a combination of design defects and aging issues that must be addressed to ensure reliable operation into the future and to restore, or surpass, original design-requirements performance. The highest priority is the refurbishment of the A2 cells, followed by the A2 injector and pulsed power systems. The VCSs procured during the initial DARHT construction project have accumulated an average of ten hydro detonations each, with an intended design life of ten.
